business.description: Likhitha Infrastructure Limited is an Oil and Gas Infrastructure Company with 28 years of experience in pipeline construction and associated facilities. The Company undertakes cross-country pipeline projects, city gas distribution networks, storage terminals, and operations & maintenance services for leading energy companies in India.

products.name: Cross-Country Pipelines
products.note: Construction of cross-country pipelines for crude oil, natural gas, LPG, and petroleum products including pipeline laying, mechanical works, civil construction, electrical and instrumentation systems, testing, commissioning.

products.name: City Gas Distribution
products.note: Laying steel and MDPE pipelines, developing distribution infrastructure, providing last-mile connectivity, and constructing CNG stations for domestic, commercial, and industrial consumers.

outlook.statement: India's energy infrastructure presents significant opportunities. The Government's emphasis on expanding natural gas infrastructure, improving city gas distribution networks, and improving pipeline connectivity is expected to support sustained investment in the sector. India's natural gas demand is expected to grow significantly by 2030, supported by expanding industrial activity, increasing adoption of cleaner fuels and continued investment in gas infrastructure.

The increasing penetration of natural gas, expansion of City Gas Distribution networks, development of pipeline connectivity and the broader requirement for energy infrastructure are expected to create opportunities across our areas of expertise. The Company will continue to leverage its experience, technical capabilities and customer relationships to participate in this growth and strengthen its position in the sector.

The Company is gradually expanding its operations beyond India. Presence in Abu Dhabi, UAE and Saudi Arabia provides a foundation for developing international business in a measured manner. The approach to international growth will remain consistent with principles that have guided the Company in India - focus on projects where we have necessary capabilities, where risks are understood and manageable, and where successful execution can create sustainable value.

Continued investments in energy infrastructure, natural gas transmission and City Gas Distribution networks are expected to support long-term demand for pipeline construction services. With its proven execution track record and domain expertise, Likhitha Infrastructure Limited is well positioned to participate in this growth while delivering sustainable value to its stakeholders.

India's continued investment in energy infrastructure is expected to support steady demand for oil and gas pipeline projects over the coming years. Expansion of natural gas transmission networks, refinery and petrochemical capacity, and city gas infrastructure will continue to generate opportunities for engineering and construction companies with proven execution capabilities.

The Middle East continues to invest heavily in oil and gas infrastructure as countries strengthen energy security, expand natural gas production and diversify their economies. Key projects, including the expansion of the Jafurah Gas Field and the Master Gas System, are expected to create sustained demand for pipeline engineering and construction services.
The Company is exploring opportunities in the Middle East and has registered a Joint Venture in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to further expand its presence.

Government of India initiatives promoting gas-based economy, Unified Tariff system under 'One Nation, One Grid', 100% FDI in gas infrastructure, ₹67,000 crore allocated for expanding National Gas infrastructure including Urja Ganga project, and Green Hydrogen Mission with planned investment of ₹17,490 crores till 2030.

orders_or_contracts.statement: Order book of over ₹1,454 crore provides a platform for future execution and reflects the trust placed in the Company by its customers.
Subsequent to the close of the financial year, the award of ₹510 crore contract from CPECC-Abu Dhabi for Pipeline Package-1 of the ASAB project marked an important milestone for the Company.
Order book exceeding ₹850 crores as on 31st March 2026, comprising a diversified mix of cross-country pipelines, City Gas Distribution (CGD) networks, and tankage terminal projects.

Secured largest international order to date valued at approximately ₹510 crores (USD 54 million) from China Petroleum Engineering & Construction Corporation for the Pipeline Package-1 (ASAB) in recent developments following the close of the financial year.

Successfully commissioned the Krishnapatnam–Hyderabad Petroleum Products Pipeline (KHPL), completed the Nagpur–Chhindwara–Jabalpur (NCJPL) pipeline across environmentally sensitive terrain, and achieved successful hydro-testing of a long-distance stretch of the Mumbai–Nagpur–Jharsuguda (MNJPL) pipeline.

Government policies

Input costs

Execution risks
Project execution dependent on external factors such as land acquisition, statutory approvals and right-of-way clearances managed by project owners and regulatory authorities
Fluctuations in prices of key inputs including steel and polyethylene pipes can influence project costs and margins
Executing projects across multiple locations requires seamless coordination of manpower, equipment, logistics and vendor networks
Occupational Health & Safety: Pipeline construction involves high-risk activities across varied terrains and operating environments
Human Resource Risk: Growth depends on attracting, retaining and developing skilled professionals across project locations
Competition Risk: Infrastructure sector remains highly competitive with project awards driven by technical knowhow, financial strength, execution track record and pricing
Regulatory Risk: Infrastructure projects operate in a complex regulatory manner involving multiple statutory approvals, environmental requirements and contractual obligations
Liquidity Risk: Delays in customer collections, changes in working capital requirements or unforeseen market conditions could impact liquidity and cash flows
Cyber Security & Data Privacy: Increasing digitalisation exposes businesses to cyber threats, unauthorised access, data breaches and operational disruptions
International Operations: Managing risks arising from foreign exchange movements and geopolitical developments
Any future pandemic lock-down extensions would affect operations

The Company has formulated a Risk Assessment and Management Policy and has in place a mechanism to identify various elements of risks, which, in the opinion of the Board, may threaten the existence of the Company and contains measures to mitigate the same.
